title: One entrance round the door: three ways to carry the spoil out
question: Which of these reads most like the nest you want, and is one entrance worth a much smaller nest? Or may the lift carry spoil out to the door (your 2026-08-31 placement ruling)?
context_md:
Since the granary shipped, a colony under the five-column door opens 6-7 entrances where the old strip allowed 2. Traced: **the roof breaks under the colony's own spoil heaps**. A dug pellet is posted straight up over its gallery, so every gallery grows a heap, and the heap cue cannot see a cut under a heap (314 of 444 crust breaks). The storeroom adds no entrances.

Same colony, seed 2 (on each arm's median), 40 ants in digbox, frames 6,000 / 12,000 / 18,000 / 24,000. Medians over 24 seeds:

| | entrances at 40 ants | cells dug | entrances at 200 ants | cells dug |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| shipped | 6.5 | 204 | 9.5 | 618 |
| walk it out | **1** | 41 | **3** | 74 |
| walk it out and back | **2** | 51 | 7 | 304 |
| lift it out the nearest hole | 5 | 286 | 12 | 764 |

Not built: the lift carrying spoil to the door. It would put the heaps at the door and keep the diggers at their faces, but it is a rule about where the colony's spoil lands, which you ruled against. All three built forms are switches, off. Report: .
